tasks.short: Budget security operations from posted lines

steps.what: Open stored lines for security budgets
Draft the operations budget from stored lines

loop.purpose: Draft an operations budget that cites only posted cost lines.
loop.input: Posted cost line id, amount, and period.
loop.output: A draft budget whose every line cites a stored id.
loop.check: Every cited id exists, and no amount is typed by the draft.
loop.stop: Stop when a line has no stored id or the period has no rows.
loop.why_not_simpler: A blank form cannot show which posted lines were left out.

tasks.design: Posted cost lines sit on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A draft budget cites only those lines. The security manager accepts the total, and the file step stores that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budgets lived in mailed sheets, so a new period was retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Posted lines can be listed, and a draft can be limited to their identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: A cost that is not posted still has to be judged and typed.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which operations the lines do not cover.

ambition.what: A posted cost change can refresh the draft the same week, and an unchecked total is not filed.

tasks.altitude: The week is spent on which operations to fund, once the lines are already listed.

evidence.claim: A budget can be drafted from posted cost lines, and a person accepts the total. The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person.

assumptions: The work starts when a budget period opens and ends when the accepted operations budget is filed.
Each line has an id, an amount, and a period, produced by the finance posting. A missing line is typed by the manager and is not drafted.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether security costs are already posted as separate lines.
research_questions: Which cost types are still outside the posting?

already_counted.description: Checking the draft is already in the decision step.

incremental.description: Retire a draft when a posted line changes.

approvals.approved_version: budget lines the manager accepted for that period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when costs are not posted as lines. The manager still accepts the total. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate security breaches before resolving them

steps.what: Decide whether that breach is resolved
Record the resolution on the breach log

tasks.design: Open alerts are listed from the {OPS_SYSTEM} log. The security manager investigates and decides whether a breach is resolved. The log stores that decision and does not close an alert by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alerts arrived in messages, and the same breach was chased twice.
tasks.enabler_now: An alert log can list what is still open.
tasks.still_hard: Whether an event is a real breach, and whether it is over, stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager has the site context the log does not.

ambition.what: An open alert is reviewed the same shift, and it is not marked resolved until the manager decides.

tasks.altitude: The week moves from hunting duplicate alerts to deciding which breach is still open.

reach.task: Act on a breach marked resolved
reach.learn: Which alert was left open and why

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person.

Closing a breach can affect staff or guests. The source pack names a rule that a significant decision about a person is not taken by automation alone, and that hiring, appraisal, or staff monitoring needs works-council consent. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a breach alert is logged and ends when the manager's resolution is stored on that alert.
An alert has an id, a time, a place, and a short type, produced by the alarm or the person who logged it. An alert without those fields stays on the open list and is not auto-closed.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether alarms already write a row, or only a phone call.
research_questions: Which alert types are logged today, and which are only spoken?

already_counted.description: The investigation time is already in the investigate step.

incremental.description: Retire a resolution if a new event arrives on the same alert.

approvals.approved_version: resolution the manager decided for that alert

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when alerts are phone calls with no row. A listed alert is not treated as resolved. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct on-site security for people and property

steps.what: List security activities to coordinate today
Direct security activities on company property

tasks.design: Today's posts are listed from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Directing activities on the property, and noting which posts safeguard guests, stay with the security manager. The list does not assign people by a score.
tasks.previous_blocker: The day's posts were a handwritten sheet that went stale by noon.
tasks.enabler_now: A roster can show who is already posted.
tasks.still_hard: Directing people on the property cannot be done from a list.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees guests and gaps the roster does not.
tasks.altitude: The week still starts on the property. The list only removes the hunt for who is posted.

reach.task: Hold the post the manager named

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person. Directing posts is not a score of the people on them.

The source pack names a rule that a significant decision about a person is not taken by automation alone, and that hiring, appraisal, or staff monitoring needs works-council consent. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when the day's posts are known and ends when the manager has directed the activities and noted the guest posts.
A post row has a place, a time, and a person id, produced by the roster. A missing row is filled on site and is not invented.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether posts are rostered in a system or only on paper.
research_questions: Who is allowed to see the post roster?

already_counted.description: Time on the property is already in the directing step.

incremental.description: Update the activity list when a post changes during the day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the roster is paper. Directing people stays in person. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct emergency management and contingency planning

steps.what: Direct contingency planning with duty leads

tasks.design: The current plan is opened from {DOCS}. The security manager directs the planning with duty leads. Only actions agreed in that meeting are recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans sat in old files, and the meeting rebuilt them from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: The current plan can be opened as a single document.
tasks.still_hard: Emergency management is a conversation about what the site can actually do.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which actions the site cannot perform.
tasks.altitude: Planning meetings start from the current plan instead of a blank page.

reach.task: Carry out an agreed emergency action

evidence.claim: The source pack says security work in this group is ticket and incident-log configuration, and that the judgement stays with a person.

assumptions: The work starts when a contingency review is called and ends when the agreed emergency actions are recorded.
The plan is one document with a version and dated actions, produced by the last signed review. A missing plan is written in the meeting and is not generated.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the security manager's effort.
A draft that cites an identifier which is not in the store is discarded.
The incremental hours retire stale drafts when source rows change.
unknowns: Whether a current contingency plan exists as a document.
research_questions: Who must be in the room before an action is treated as agreed?

already_counted.description: The planning meeting is already in the directing step.

incremental.description: Retire an action when the site layout changes.

approvals.approved_version: actions agreed in that planning meeting

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when there is no current plan. The meeting stays. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Budgets use posted lines, and a breach alert is not resolved until the manager decides. Directing people on the property, and emergency planning, stay with the security manager.
reach: Finance sees the filed budget, not the draft.
A duty lead sees which alert stayed open.
skills_to_grow: Refuse a budget line that is not posted.
Do not mark a breach resolved from the alert alone.
role.ambitious_version: A cost change refreshes the draft the same week, and an alert is still reviewed by a person the same shift.
